_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.
_meta.maintenance: Manual updates + Claude WebSearch each session. 2026-08-03 refresh: Japan MoF/BoJ conducted ~$34B USDJPY intervention Thursday-Friday (US-coordinated per Bloomberg); suspected second intervention today drove JPY +1.18% to 155.20. Yen was at 40-year low pre-intervention. This replaces the Iran-pause theme as the primary JPY driver — haven-fading story from Jul 27 is now stale, JPY strength is now intervention-driven not organic. Warsh Fed + USMCA themes still current.

themes.title: Japan FX intervention regime — ~$34B spent Thu/Fri + suspected re-entry Aug 3, US-coordinated
themes.summary: Japan MoF spent ~$34B (¥5.33T) intervening in USDJPY on Thursday, first intervention in ~3 months. Suspected second intervention today (Aug 3) drove JPY +1.18% to 155.20 — strongest since early May. Bloomberg reports US Treasury coordination with Japan — this is the critical piece. Coordinated interventions historically STICK because two central banks defending a level scares off short-term shorts. Backdrop: yen had hit 40-year low earlier July under pressure from Iran-war energy costs + fiscal concerns + wide rate differentials. BOJ held policy rate at 1% (highest since 1995) at last meeting — but rate policy is secondary to intervention story right now. Net regime: JPY strength is manufactured, not organic. Doesn't matter for medium-term direction — intervention typically buys 2-5 trading days of directional force before mean-reversion pressures build.

implications.JPY: STRONG tailwind — coordinated US-Japan intervention is defending yen. All JPY-cross SHORTS get an active tailwind; JPY-cross LONGS are fighting central-bank action (very risky). This overrides the Warsh-Fed carry-gap headwind theme in the short term.
implications.USD: USDJPY specifically is under intervention pressure DOWN. Other USD pairs unaffected by JPY intervention directly, but USD/JPY move flows into broader dollar sentiment (soft DXY).
implications.CAD: no direct effect from intervention; USMCA + oil pause still dominate CAD.
implications.AUD: indirect: JPY-cross shorts (AUDJPY down) hurt AUD longs; AUD/USD relatively unaffected.
implications.EUR: EUR/JPY down; watch for spillover into EUR/USD if intervention creates broader risk-off tone.
implications.GBP: GBP/JPY down; similar spillover risk to EUR.
implications.CHF: CHF/JPY under pressure; independent CHF weakness (SNB / unwind of Iran-haven bid) compounds

themes.watchLevel: USD/JPY sustained BELOW 150 = intervention doing serious damage, extend JPY-strong bias. USD/JPY BACK ABOVE 158 = intervention effect exhausted, market pushing back hard, exit JPY longs / prepare for reversal. Any Kanda/MoF official statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately.

themes.title: Warsh Fed hawkish — 5th consecutive hold expected, 9/18 forecast a 2026 hike
themes.summary: Kevin Warsh (Fed Chair since May) sticking with hawkish framing at July FOMC. Rates held 3.5-3.75% for fifth straight meeting. June CPI declined -0.4% m/m taking annual to 3.5% (from 4.2% May) — cooling but Warsh has explicitly said FOMC has 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.' Median year-end 2026 rate forecast raised to 3.8% (from 3.4%); 9 of 18 members now expect at least one hike this year. Traditional forward guidance eliminated — pure data-dependent. Net: USD carry stays firm, hike risk is one-sided (higher, not lower). NOTE: for USDJPY specifically, this theme is currently OVERRIDDEN by active Japan FX intervention pushing the pair down against carry differential.

implications.USD: STRUCTURAL tailwind — hawkish Warsh + hike-tilted dots = USD carry defended (except vs JPY, see intervention theme)
implications.JPY: STRUCTURAL headwind BUT currently overridden by intervention — do not trade USDJPY on this thesis alone right now
implications.EUR: headwind — ECB cutting while Fed holds hawkish widens rate diff against EUR
implications.GBP: headwind — BoE also cutting; USD carry differential works vs GBP too
implications.CAD: mixed — USD strength offsets oil support; USDCAD structurally biased up unless oil rerates
implications.AUD: headwind — RBA on hold with easing bias; carry disadvantaged vs USD

themes.watchLevel: Any hint of Warsh softening in speeches = pivot back in play, unwinds this theme. Sub-3.0% Y/Y CPI print = dovish tolerance returns. DXY closing below 100 = market rejecting hawkish read.

themes.title: USMCA review live + Section 122 Mexico surcharge — binary CAD event
themes.summary: Two live threads. (1) USMCA joint review opened Jul 1 — Trump said 'not renewing in current form.' First US-Mexico bilateral round done May, tackled auto rules of origin + steel/alu + economic security. (2) Section 122 10% Mexico surcharge (imposed after SCOTUS struck down IEEPA tariffs Feb 20) expiry window Jul 24 — extension/replacement decision still pending as of Aug 3. Extension mechanism, replacement action, or lapse each move CAD/MXN differently. Result: CAD trades in a headline-driven regime with binary risk that could hit within days.

implications.CAD: elevated vol BOTH directions — surcharge status + USMCA framing decisions land in a compressed window. Wider SLs, smaller sizes on CAD-crosses.
implications.USD: moderate vol — indirect via trade-policy narrative; less directly hit than CAD/MXN
implications.MXN: highest exposure (not in book) — but MXN moves telegraph CAD next-day

themes.watchLevel: Section 122 formal extension proclamation OR clean lapse resolves half the theme. USMCA renewal terms announcement resolves the other half. Watch for USDMXN / USDCAD gaps on any Trump trade-policy speech.
